record.title: Barak exclave's Ak-Tash–Birlishken route restriction continuing into 2018
record.scope: Ordinary direct passage by Barak residents
record.direction: Resident movement in both directions; not all nationalities or commercial categories
record.movement: Barak residents using the nearest connection to mainland Kyrgyzstan
record.exceptions: Emergency passage was agreed in 2013; authorised supplies continued during 2013–2015. Later practice is not fully reconstructed.
record.imposing_authority: Uzbek border authorities, as attributed by DCAF; bilateral authorities negotiated restoration
record.enforcement: Ordinary local passage suspended; restored operation is asserted retrospectively by the government.
record.consequences: Residents described difficult detours; research links isolation to departures from the enclave.
record.relationship: Distinct crossing from Madaniyat, Baymak, Kara-Suu and Rishtan–Sokh. Inherited restriction qualifies because sources describe persistence into 2018.
record.status_observation: Evidence is limited to the reported episode; no present-day status is inferred.
record.official_rationale: Contemporary reporting attributes the Ak-Tash restriction to absence from the agreed bilateral checkpoint roster, pending legalization; original Uzbek instruction not retrieved.
record.context: An enclave-access restriction inherited into the study window; residents could use a much longer alternative route.
record.uncertainty: Year-only onset reconciles a February 2013 emergency-only account with later 'spring 2013' wording. December 25 is an official operational assertion, not independent traveller observation. Reopening was resident-specific. Government copies and DCAF's cited Fergana account share lineage.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Unknown onset day, supply/emergency exceptions and resident-limited endpoint preclude a uniform duration.

followup_reviews.Challenge finding: The source attributes refusal to reopen to absence from an agreed checkpoint list. Its general reference to disputed questions and proposed PM-level discussions does not establish opposing government positions, territorial claims, retaliation or coercive pressure. I_general requires a recorded interstate/inter-authority dispute, not merely a bilateral legal-authorization problem. Keep the attributed reason, leave assignments empty, and explicitly mark known reason outside taxonomy. FUQ-168 can be resolved for the known stated reason without asserting all underlying motives are known.
followup_reviews.Root decision: Root reviewed the saved research, current claims and separate challenge. Accepted with challenge corrections. followup_reviews.Issue dispositions: FUQ-168 — resolved: The attributed immediate explanation is known: Ak-Tash lacked bilateral authorization and would remain restricted pending legalization. The generic missing-rationale issue is therefore resolved without a code.
